svg.title: FFN receive layouts: expert and token
svg.desc: Two Attention GPUs dispatch four tokens, each with three expert choices, to two FFN GPUs. FFN GPU 0 receives three of them. The expert layout copies a token once per local expert and groups rows by expert. The token layout keeps one row per token with local expert IDs and weights; ID -1 and weight 0 mark an expert on another GPU and unused rows, written by the copy kernel.
svg.text: What an FFN GPU receives: expert layout or token layout

g.text: once per FFN GPU: x + 3 IDs + 3 weights
t1: all 3 experts on FFN GPU 1
Expert layout - what FFN GPU 0 receives
One row per (token, local expert): tokens are copied
= 2 Attention GPUs x 2 tokens x 3 experts
Token layout - what FFN GPU 0 receives
One row per token; columns = its 3 chosen experts (top_k), not GPUs
ID -1, weight 0 = skip: expert is on another GPU, or row is unused
e.g. t0 chose e1, e5, e2; e5 is on FFN GPU 1, which runs it
Attention GPUs sum each token's reply rows from all FFN GPUs
source_collect(): same output in both layouts
local expert: stored as ID - first local ID
expert on another GPU: ID -1, weight 0
When tokens are copied into recv_x
Across NVLink domains: how t0 reaches both FFN GPUs
The token record is the same in both layouts and both modes: x + 3 IDs + 3 weights. Only the receiving GPU's copy kernel differs.
